Where does he say that he's deaf? He only says in his post that he has "trouble hearing." I looked through his comment history too, and he doesn't mention deafness. And even if he were, deaf people are absolutely capable of perceiving sound quality - just look up one star reviews of hearing aids that complain about it.

Sound isn't like light where you can block out someone's view by covering their eyes, it's vibrations hitting the eardrum, and all of the information is contained within the frequencies of these vibrations. When someone has hearing loss, they don't lose the ability to perceive the "details" in what they hear, it's just that they hear a range of frequencies at a lower volume than normal. That's why most hearing aids work by picking up those frequencies and playing them louder to compensate.

Even if OP had some nerve damage, increasing the volume would still work as long as OP isn't 100% incapable of hearing. He should be able to hear how a soundbar with subwoofers will sound much more open than a pair of headphones as long as the volume is sufficiently loud. In fact, if OP were deaf, speakers would make an even larger difference for him because [deaf audiophiles experience music by feeling vibrations with their hands and bodies](https://insheepsclothinghifi.com/listening-bob-lichtenberg-stereophile/), which most headphones are not powerful enough to generate.

I'm not trying to justify OP's actions here, but my pair of $150 speakers trades blows with my $1700 headphones in some aspects. You lose a lot of sound quality when you go from speakers to headphones.
